note: Words for the in-app help pages: the hub, the tutorial, the how-to guides and the list of technical documents. Fictional ACME demonstration wording only. Screen labels in the steps are copied from the screens. The tutorial and the guides state no fee, limit or rule; those come from rules_and_fees.json.

tutorial.title: Tutorial: the demo story
tutorial.intro: The story follows one fence permit through the City. An applicant applies, an agent operator wakes the agents that prepare the case, a data steward settles a question about who the applicant is, a permit reviewer checks the application and records a decision, and a city administrator tests a rule change. Each section is for one person. The numbered steps use the labels you see on the screens.
tutorial.switch_note: You act as one person at a time. To change person, open Demo controls and pick the next one. The tutorial does not switch for you.
tutorial.replay_note: Muse is the AI model that drafts answers in this demonstration. Where a step shows a Muse answer, it is a recorded replay: a stored answer shown again, and its label says so. No model is called when you follow these steps.
tutorial.state_note: Some screens are empty until the demo data is prepared. The steps say when. If a list is empty, ask whoever runs the demo to prepare the data as the user test guide describes in the technical documentation.

sections.intro: The applicant is a resident who wants to put up a fence. You use the City of Acme website, which has its own menu apart from the staff screens.

steps.do: Open "Demo controls" and choose "Applicant".
steps.see: You land on the City of Acme home page, signed in as the applicant.

steps.do: Click "Apply for a permit".
steps.see: The "Permits and applications" page opens.

steps.do: Click "Start an application".
steps.see: The page "Start an application" lists the permit types as cards.

steps.do: Click the "Residential deck or fence" card.
steps.see: The application form opens.

steps.do: Choose "Fence". Type the property address "400 Lantern Row" and pick the suggested address. Type the fence height 6. Leave the rest blank.
steps.see: The form accepts what you typed. Nothing is saved until you press "Submit application".

steps.do: Click "Submit application".
steps.see: A summary headed "There is a problem" lists every missing item, and a message sits beside each field. Everything you typed is kept.

steps.do: Fix each item: Fence material cedar; Location on the property "Side or rear yard"; Distance from the property line 2; tick "I will not build over the property line"; add a Project description; Email demo.applicant@example.invalid; add a Site sketch and a Material specification with "Add file" (a small text file works); tick the certification.
steps.see: Each message beside a field goes away once the field is complete.

steps.do: Click "Submit application" again.
steps.see: A receipt headed "Application received" shows your reference number and the status "Awaiting intake agent".

steps.do: Click "Track application", or "My permits" in the top menu.
steps.see: "My permits" lists your applications under the tabs Active, Drafts and Closed.

steps.do: Click "Start an application", then "Residential deck or fence". Click "Ask" at the corner of the page, type "Do I need a permit for a 6 ft fence?" under "Your question" and click "Ask".
steps.see: The answer shows the label "Recorded demo answer" and cites ACME Code §14-305 and §14-306. It is a stored answer that was shown again.

sections.intro: The agent operator wakes the intake agent, asks it to prepare the fence case, and reads what it did. An agent proposes and a person decides: the operator makes no permit decision. The operator also wakes and runs the steward assistant; the Data Steward still decides every recommendation. Leave the steward assistant awake for the next section.

steps.do: Open "Demo controls" and choose "Agent Operator".
steps.see: You land on "Agents". The counts read "Waiting", "Running" and "Failed". Under "Agent status" the Intake agent reads asleep.

steps.do: Click "Intake agent" in the left menu.
steps.see: The page says "The agent is asleep, so the run buttons are off." Open "More details" to read "Processing" and "Engine".

steps.do: Click "Wake agent".
steps.see: The button now reads "Put agent to sleep". The batch button reads Process N cases, or Process the next 20 of N when more than 20 cases are waiting.

steps.do: Under "Waiting work", click "Process one" on the fence case, or press the batch button. It reads Process N cases, or Process the next 20 of N when more than 20 cases are waiting.
steps.see: The case leaves the table. Open "More details" and read "Recent results". If the table says "Nothing is waiting for this agent.", send an application as the Applicant first.

steps.do: Open "Agent runs" in the left menu, then click "View run" on the row for the fence case.
steps.see: "Run detail" shows "Processing mode", "Processing steps" and "Recorded business changes". These runs use "Built in logic". No model was called.

steps.do: Open "Steward assistant" in the left menu and click "Wake agent". Leave it awake.
steps.see: The steward assistant reads awake. Click "Prepare recommendations" to prepare the work of the queue, or leave it to the Data Steward.

sections.intro: The data steward keeps the records of people, organizations and properties right. Here the steward clears the fence case so a reviewer can decide it. The steward assistant only proposes. The steward records the decision.

steps.do: Open "Demo controls" and choose "Data Steward".
steps.see: You land on "Data issues".

steps.do: Click "Prepare recommendations".
steps.see: Each task the assistant works on gets a "High", "Review" or "Held" pill and a one line reason. If the button is off, the Agent Operator has not woken the "Steward assistant".

steps.do: Open the "Check the property" issue that names the fence case. Click "Start" under "Approve parcel link", write a "Decision note" and submit it.
steps.see: The page records the decision. The parcel link is approved. The permit is not approved.

steps.do: Open the "Check the person identity" issue from "ACME ePermit Portal (simulated)". Click "Start" under "Confirm link to Demo Applicant", write a "Decision note" and submit it.
steps.see: The page records the decision. Without this approval and the parcel approval, a later approval is refused.

steps.do: Click "Master records" in the left menu and open the tab "People and organizations".
steps.see: The list shows the master records. A master record is the one agreed version of a person or organization.

sections.intro: The permit reviewer checks the fence case against the rules and records a decision. Deciding and issuing are separate. This path records the decision directly. Confirm the recommendation and Revert the recommendation appear only after the adjudication agent has left a recommendation.

steps.do: Open "Demo controls" and choose "Permit Reviewer".
steps.see: You land on the "Work queue".

steps.do: Open "Review queue" and open the fence case.
steps.see: The permit workspace opens for that application.

steps.do: Click the tabs "Documents", "People and organizations", "Activity" and "Review" in turn.
steps.see: Each tab shows one part of the case: the files sent in, the people and the organizations, what has happened, and the review.

steps.do: On the "People and organizations" tab, click "Start" under "Confirm parcel" and submit it.
steps.see: The page updates in place and keeps the tab.

steps.do: On the "Review" tab, click "Start" under "Run application checks" and submit it.
steps.see: The rule results appear. An open parcel or identity link is Data follow-up: it is separate from the rule results and does not refuse the decision.

steps.do: Click "Start" under "Record review decision". Choose "Approve", write the "Rationale (internal record)" and click "Record the decision".
steps.see: An open parcel or identity link does not refuse the approval. The case shows Data follow-up, and the Data Steward can confirm it afterwards. A check that was not run because the parcel is not confirmed is listed as Not checked; the reviewer decides whether to approve against it and records an exception reason when required. After an approval, "Issue permit" is refused until the fee is assessed, paid and reconciled. The payer account is still required to apply a payment and to issue.

sections.intro: The city administrator tests a rule change on past cases before anyone changes a rule, then looks at how the City is doing.

steps.do: Open "Demo controls" and choose "City Administrator".
steps.see: You land on the planning overview.

steps.do: Open "More tools" in the left menu, then click "What-if".
steps.see: The page lists suggestions and your saved what-ifs.

steps.do: Under "Start from a suggestion" click "Raise the side/rear fence height limit from 6 ft to 7 ft".
steps.see: The editor opens. When the synthetic year (sample data) is loaded, the seed 20261028 and the case count 600 are already filled in.

steps.do: Click "Run what-if".
steps.see: The results page compares the current rule with the change. With the prepared sample data, 600 cases are tested and 28 of them change outcome: approvals go from 306 to 334 and denials from 80 to 52.

steps.do: Click "Read briefing". When live Muse is on, click "Write the briefing with Muse". When it is off, click "Try recorded Muse briefing".
steps.see: When the call is live the label reads "Muse briefing (live)". When it is a recorded answer the label reads "Recorded Muse briefing". The sections are "Summary", "Key effects", and "Risks and trade-offs". The hosted demonstration allows 100 live Muse calls a day. When that allowance is used up, the recorded answer is used.

steps.do: Go back to the results page and click "Save as a draft rule change".
steps.see: The change is saved as a draft with the status "Draft: ready for your approval". Click "Open the draft" to approve and publish it on Rules and fees. If your city uses independent approval, the status reads "Draft: needs independent approval" and the reason beside the disabled buttons says you authored this version: another administrator must approve it, and another must publish it.

steps.do: Open "More tools" in the left menu, then open "City view", "Operations dashboard", "Audit log", "Support" and "Checks".
steps.see: Each page loads. The Operations dashboard shows the figures, and the Audit log shows what each person and system did.

howto.intro: Each guide covers one task in 5 to 10 steps. The labels are the ones on the screens. Guides for your own role are listed first.

guides.title: Apply for a fence or deck permit
guides.summary: Fill in the application, fix what the form points out, and send it.
steps: Open the City website and click "Apply for a permit", then click "Start an application" on the Permits page. On the application pages, "Start an application" is also in the top menu.
Click the "Residential deck or fence" card.
Choose "Fence" or "Deck" and type the property address and the size or height.
Press "Submit application" even if the form is not complete. It never stays disabled. A summary headed "There is a problem" lists what is missing and a message sits beside each field.
Fill in the missing items. Fields marked * are required, and optional fields say "(optional)".
Add the files with "Add file": a site sketch and a material specification.
Tick "I will not build over the property line" and the certification.
Press "Submit application". A receipt headed "Application received" shows your reference number.
guides.result: The status is "Awaiting intake agent". Keep the reference number to find the application later.

guides.title: Track an application and answer a request for information
guides.summary: See where an application stands and send the City what it asks for.
steps: Click "Track or resume an application" on the Permits page, or click "My permits" in the top menu of an application page. Applications are listed under the tabs Active, Drafts and Closed.
To find one by number, type it in "Find an application by reference number" and click "Track".
Read the progress steps and the status on the application card.
If the City has asked for something, a box on the card names the request. Click "View request" to read it.
On the application page read "Messages from the City" and "What the City asked".
Under "Submit revised documents" add the files the City asked for and click "Submit revised documents".
Under "Send the answer back to the City" check the files and click "Send the answer to the City".
Read the confirmation. The City assesses the application again from the start.
guides.result: The application goes back to the City with a new revision. The original submission time is kept.

guides.title: Ask the help assistant and ask the City
guides.summary: Get a cited answer about a permit, or send a question to a person at the City.
steps: Open "Start an application", "My permits" or an application form, and click "Ask" at the corner of the page, or "Ask about your permit" in the header. The assistant opens over the page.
Type your question under "Your question", for example "Do I need a permit for a 6 ft fence?"
Click "Ask". You can also click one of the questions the City is often asked.
Read the answer. Its label says where it came from. In this demonstration it reads "Recorded demo answer".
Open a citation, such as ACME Code §14-306, and click "Show the rule text" to read the rule the answer relies on.
If the assistant did not answer, the panel says so and shows the rule text that matches your words.
To reach a person, open "Contact the City" from the menu of the City website, type under "Your question" and click "Send my question".
Find your request, and the City's answer to it, on the contact page and under "More details" in the panel.
guides.result: The assistant explains the published rules and never decides a permit. A person at the City answers the request you send.

guides.title: Review an application and record a decision
guides.summary: Run the rule checks on a case and record the outcome with a reason.
steps: Open "Review queue". Read "Stage" and "Next action" for each case. Stage shows where the case is, for example "Checks (3 of 6)". Next action is what is needed now: "Ready to decide", "Ready to issue", "Needs checks", "Fee not settled", "In early resolution" or "Submitted with known issues". "Ready to decide" and "Ready to issue" come first. An open parcel or identity link is a "Data follow-up" tag, not the next-action blocker. To find one case, type its reference, the applicant name or the site address in Search and press Search. A number such as 617 matches SYN-APP-617. Tags on the row show what the agents recommend, and a chip filters to one tag. Click the reference of a case.
Read the tabs "Documents", "People and organizations", "Activity" and "Review".
On the "People and organizations" tab, click "Start" under "Confirm parcel" and submit it.
On the "Review" tab, click "Start" under "Run application checks" and submit the form.

Read the rule results. An open parcel or identity link is Data follow-up and does not have to be settled before the decision. A check listed as Not checked needs an exception reason before you approve. The payer account and the fee still have to be settled before the permit is issued.
Click "Start" under "Record review decision".
Choose "Approve", "Approve with conditions" or "Deny". For a denial also choose the "Denial reason code".
Write the "Rationale (internal record)". It is required.
Click "Record the decision" and read the message at the top.
guides.result: The decision is recorded against the versions you saw. Data follow-up does not refuse it. Another blocker, such as an expired credential or a stale check, still refuses an approval and says why. Issue permit stays refused until the fee is assessed, paid and reconciled.

guides.title: Resolve a data issue (the Cedarline example)
guides.summary: Decide whether two similar records are the same organization.
steps: Click "Data issues" in the left menu. With the Cedarline demonstration data loaded, "Needs review" lists 3 cases.
Open the case for ERP-BL-00413 (Cedarline Coffee Works).
Read the sections 1 to 4 in order. Section 3 compares the source record with each master record it might belong to. Section 4 lists what agrees and what conflicts.
Look at Cedarline Coffee Roasters LLC, the near-duplicate. Its name, license number and unit all conflict with the source record. A similar name is not the same organization.
Under "5. What will this action do?" read the preview of each action. The guide's answer for the near-duplicate is "Reject match": never confirm a link to Cedarline Coffee Roasters LLC.
Click "Reject match", then "Start". Write a Decision note that names the conflicts, and submit.
Read the message and the section "6. What happened?".

If a candidate agrees on every compared field, as Cedarline Coffee Works LLC does for this record, choose it under "Compare with" and press "Show this record". The case then offers "Confirm link to Cedarline Coffee Works LLC". Choose the action that matches the evidence.
guides.result: A rejected match links nothing, and the source record keeps all its values. Another candidate can be linked by proposing again.

guides.title: Run a what-if and write the briefing
guides.summary: Test a rule change on sample cases and produce a briefing for a decision maker.
steps: Open "More tools" in the left menu, then click "What-if".
Under "Start from a suggestion" click "Raise the side/rear fence height limit from 6 ft to 7 ft", or build your own under "Or start empty".
In "Run this what-if" check the Population, the Seed and the Number of cases.
Click "Run what-if".
Read "Recommendation by outcome, baseline and scenario" and "Cases that change, and which way".
Click "Legislator briefing".
Click "Write the briefing with Muse". The source label shows whether the text is a recorded replay.
Read the sections, then use "Download (HTML)" or "Download (Markdown)" if you need a copy.
guides.result: The figures come from the rule engine. Muse only explains them. When live Muse is off, or the daily allowance of 100 calls is used up, the briefing is a recorded answer and the label says so.

guides.title: Propose and approve a rule change
guides.summary: Turn a what-if into a draft and take it through approval and publication. Under the single-administrator policy you can do every step yourself.
steps: Run a what-if as described in the guide on what-ifs.
On the results page, under "Path to a real change", click "Save as a draft rule change".
Read the table. The draft is in force nowhere. It lists its author and who can approve it.
Click "Open the draft", or open "Rules and fees" in the left menu and choose the view Drafts.
Select the draft version and click "Submit for review".
Click "Approve version". Tick the box that confirms you wrote the version, give a reason and submit. The record says "Approved by the author (single-administrator policy)".
Click "Publish version". The draft becomes the version in force.

The line "Approval policy: single administrator" at the top of Rules and fees shows which policy applies. A city can switch to independent approval. Then the author of a version cannot approve or publish it, the buttons "Approve version" and "Publish version" are guarded for the author, and the reason reads "You authored this version; another administrator must approve it." beside "Approve version" and "You authored this version; another administrator must publish it." beside "Publish version". A second administrator then does both steps.
guides.result: Nothing changes in the live rules until the version is approved and published. Under the single-administrator policy, which is the default, one City Administrator can do all of it with the demo persona, and the history and the audit log record that the author approved it. The city sets the policy in config/approval_policy.json, and the environment variable ACME_APPROVAL_POLICY overrides it.

guides.title: Reconcile a payment
guides.summary: Assess a fee, match a payment to it and confirm the balance.
steps: Click "Reconciliation" in the left menu.
Find the assessment with "Search by application reference or assessment id" and click "Search the assessments". Click "View details" on the row.
Under "Finance actions" choose "Assess application" if none exists. Enter the Declared valuation and a Reason.
Choose "Confirm allocation". Pick the Receipt, enter the Amount and the Currency, a new Idempotency key and a Reason. An idempotency key makes sure the same request is never applied twice.
Choose "Reconcile assessment" and list the receipts.
Read "Allocation position" and "Fee lines" for the selected assessment.
Check that the balance is 0.00 and the status is exact before any permit is issued.
guides.result: A permit cannot be issued without an exact, settled allocation. Partial, overpaid, reversed and unmatched payments each keep their own status and balance.

guides.title: Read the operations dashboard and the audit log
guides.summary: See how the City is doing and who did what.
steps: Open "More tools" in the left menu, then click "Operations dashboard".
Read "Figures" and "Decisions recorded, by outcome". Every figure is a count or a mean over stored rows. No model is used.
Under "Synthetic data" click "Include the synthetic history (labelled)" to add the sample year, or "Leave the synthetic history out" to remove it.
Open "More tools" in the left menu, then click "Audit log".
Narrow the list with the filters Actor type, Action and "Search (optional)", then click "Apply filters".
Click "Details" on a row to open the event in a side panel.
Use "Newer" and "Older" to move between pages, and "Clear filters" to start again.
guides.result: The audit log is read only. It records every action once and nobody can edit it.
